reviews.text: This type of establishment is supposed to be illegal. Numerous accounts of animal abuse exist. We no longer want to live in a world where animals are exploited for the profit of a few. Do the right thing, close your slave-trading business.
Cute small pet shop.

Horrible experience; I will never set foot in that pet shop again.

Absolutely no respect for animal welfare. The puppies are kept in the basement, you can hear them howling, and the smell of urine is overwhelming. I don't understand why animal welfare organizations don't visit to monitor their living conditions. It's simply shameful.
Are dogs and cats still being sold in pet shops?

Today, Sunday, the store is closed, and the puppies and kittens are locked inside. The animals' cries and barks are incessant.

According to Law No. 2021-1539 of November 30, 2021, which has been in effect since 2024, it is FORBIDDEN to sell animals in the store.

This is clearly animal abuse. Shame on those who sell them and shame on those who buy from them here.

This shop sold me a mixed-breed cat for €1600.

They claimed it was a Maine Coon, but I have no way of verifying that, as it doesn't have a pedigree certificate.

It's absolutely insane to still see this kind of shop in France, and even more so in Paris. According to law no. 2021-1539 of November 30, 2021, which has been in effect since 2024, it is FORBIDDEN to sell animals. I find this unacceptable; it's animal abuse and misinformation. Shame on those who sell them and shame on those who shop there.

We bought Vivaldi (Spitz) and were greeted by Roxane, who gave us a wonderful welcome. Roxane explained everything and gave us excellent advice.
Thank you to the whole team!
Great place! 👌🙏 …
No humanity whatsoever for animals. Locked in tiny cages, it's shameful!

We adopted our little Automne (formerly Agathe) from this pet shop and had a very pleasant experience with the whole team. We were able to meet the puppies without any problems before making our decision, so I don't understand the negative reviews about it. And our little Automne is doing perfectly well.

My daughter and I went to this pet store to buy a hamster and were shocked by the level of care provided for the animals (space, hygiene, and treatment). Upon entering the store, the overpowering smell of urine was striking, something I had never experienced in a pet store before. Everything was dirty; there were even uncleaned traces of urine on the edges of the hamster cages, on the floor, and on the counter.
We asked to see some hamsters, and they were taken out of their wire cages and placed unattended on the counter, based on the assumption that even though hamsters don't understand heights, they are strong enough to withstand falls from over a meter high, without even checking for injuries. One of them fell from the saleswoman's hands when she put it back in its cage. Surprisingly, the saleswoman seemed completely used to this. When the hamsters were taken out, we were very surprised by their extremely stressed behavior. They were trembling and avoiding our hands, something we had never seen before with our hamsters. We always let the animals approach us on their own, and something was clearly wrong.

We also saw a puppy being brought up from its cage by one of the saleswomen, and it seemed far too young to be sold in a pet shop.
I wonder what the living conditions are like downstairs?... After reading some reviews, I agree that this pet shop should not only be avoided but also reported and shut down, at least the part that sells animals, for the sake of animal welfare.
We adopted two adorable guinea pigs! We highly recommend this pet shop. Thank you so much for all your advice.

I bought two guinea pigs on January 10, 2026, thinking that since the shop was affiliated with the breeder, it would be better than buying them from a supermarket. On the day of purchase, I was told I had to buy them in pairs, even though this wasn't mentioned at all when I called the shop the day before, saying I was looking for just one guinea pig.
One of the two died that same day, January 27, 2026. After speaking with a pet store (Animalis), it seems highly likely the animals were sold at too low a weight. After careful consideration, I decided to buy another one from Animalis, which has veterinary checks every three months, and, more importantly, sells guinea pigs twice the size of those sold by this pet store, as I was able to see for myself!

For the past month and a half, we've had a perfectly healthy Morkie puppy, with no problems or hidden defects! The vet even came two days before we got him for his second vaccination. (The third vaccination was given by the same vet (very professional and thorough) the following month.)
It was easy to welcome him into our home, and we can now train him as we wish (no bad habits to report).
They are indeed kept in the back of the shop to play quietly and sleep, but we can see them when we stop by during the indicated daytime hours.
I therefore recommend the shop for obtaining a healthy and loving puppy (the owner loves what she does, and it shows!).
Very friendly welcome. Helpful advice. Shop with many accessories.

Pet stores are no longer allowed to sell dogs and cats. This pet store does it anyway. You can hear the puppies howling at night in the basement.

I bought a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel in 2015 from this pet store; they told me he was 6 months old. However, after changing veterinarians (instead of continuing with their recommended one), I was told he was only 3 months old and came from Eastern Europe, from puppy mills. This later explained the numerous health problems he had.
Your animals are exceptional
Our little treasure Perle, almost 2 years old. A wonderful dog who brings immense joy to our family. Thank you again to the animal shelter in Paris for their incredible kindness and trust.
We adopted a puppy there, he's in excellent health and very sweet. The saleswoman, Roxane, was absolutely lovely and gave us great advice. I highly recommend this pet shop! 👍👍 …
Is the sale of puppies and kittens at exorbitant prices "behind the scenes" still not prohibited?

Very friendly, welcoming, and helpful. We bought two guinea pigs (they also have some very cute rabbits). They have all the necessary accessories for all kinds of animals, dogs, cats, etc. I admit I didn't pay much attention to the food. You can also reserve animals for a week (very convenient). Thank you.

To everyone reading this: pet shop AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

Here's the story:
We bought two male guinea pigs, about 8 weeks old, from "Animaux de Paris" (babies, basically) for our son's birthday.

The saleswomen were completely detached, offering minimal information and advice, and were clearly in a hurry to close the sale. That's understandable (it's the 16th arrondissement, so I guess).

7 days later:
One of the guinea pigs suddenly died... no warning signs whatsoever. Nothing. I won't go into the details of the shock for our son (and the whole family).

So I immediately contacted the pet shop:

A DISASTER. The saleswoman on the phone kept repeating over and over that she was sorry, but that there was nothing she could do for me... even suspecting me of animal abuse. (?)

Okay... so it's normal for a baby guinea pig to die after a week??? Who are they kidding?

They simply sold us a sick animal (no veterinary check is done before the sale).

No refund or offer of a replacement. Their policy is this: they only refund if the animal dies within 48 hours... but not if it dies 7 days later. I'll let you be the judge.

This is truly SHAMEFUL.

To everyone reading this: Don't do what I did (read all the previous messages saying to avoid this pet shop and didn't), seriously, just walk away.

A guinea pig purchased from this pet shop died after only a week, despite strictly following the care instructions.

This situation was very difficult for our child, who was deeply affected by the loss of their pet.

The most shocking aspect was the staff's reaction: a complete lack of compassion, and comments implying that we had mistreated the animal, which is untrue and particularly hurtful.

We expected greater professionalism regarding the health of the animals sold, as well as a modicum of humanity towards a family and a child in distress.
A very disappointing experience.

I bought a puppy from Les Animaux de Paris last October. It was of French origin (ETCHEVERRIA kennel, LE GARRIGUET, VILLASAVARY) and came with a health certificate. Unfortunately, two days after picking him up, he fell ill with kennel cough. This is a very dangerous disease in puppies and is not considered a hidden defect, so there is no guarantee for the new owner, and the store disclaims all responsibility. After more than a month and a half of multiple courses of antibiotics, tests, x-rays, veterinary and hospital fees, and a lot of money spent, the puppy is finally starting to recover. So think carefully before buying or adopting a puppy from Les Animaux de Paris.

A disgrace to be avoided at all costs! Hygiene is appalling, guinea pigs are kept in drafts, and cages are far too small for these poor animals.
The sale of animals should be banned. This pet shop is a no-go; there is absolutely no animal welfare.

Hello,

I wanted to share my experience following my visit to the shop this morning, around 9:25 a.m.

Although the opening time was listed as 10:00 a.m., the door was open, and needing some information, I went in.

Interested in buying a dachshund puppy, I was approached by a woman who, at first glance, seemed friendly. I asked her if it was possible to see a puppy in the afternoon. Her answer: no.

Then, rather surprisingly, she asked me if I was really sure I wanted one. This way of speaking to a potential customer clearly astonished me.

She then explained that it is now "no longer allowed" to display the puppies, supposedly because some people don't think things through enough before buying. According to her, all the puppies are therefore kept in the back of the shop, with no possibility of seeing them beforehand. I've never seen anything like it!

I still asked her the price: €2,400.

At that price, it seemed perfectly normal—even essential—to be able to see the puppy before making any commitment. We're talking about a life companion, not an object.

When I asked her if I could still see one if I came back in the afternoon, she finally answered "yes," but very hesitantly.
Honestly, I left with absolutely no desire to return.

This experience left me with serious doubts about their practices and the very clear impression that money comes first.

It's a shame, because I was genuinely motivated to adopt a puppy, but I felt neither trust nor consideration.

I'm very disappointed. I had already been warned, but I didn't want to believe it. Now I understand why.

Hello,

My boyfriend and I strongly advise against this pet shop for the following reasons:

- We adopted two male guinea pigs from the pet shop two weeks ago, and both became ill immediately. One of them had a scar on his left ear on the day of adoption (not noticed by the manager, no pre-adoption check) which subsequently became infected and purulent. The second guinea pig, two days after adoption, started having runny eyes (conjunctivitis) and also had watery eyes.

- Furthermore, we immediately went to the pet shop on Tuesday (adoption on Saturday) to have them check the health of one of the guinea pigs. Their response was: "They look like small sores, but nothing serious."

- Following their advice, we waited, and the guinea pig's health deteriorated.

- After consulting the veterinarian, both animals were found to be quite ill and on antibiotics for 10 days. We requested a refund of the veterinary fees (€160) because they sold us sick animals. Despite having the necessary evidence to prove that the two guinea pigs were sick when we bought them, the manager remained firm in her position and refused to reimburse any veterinary fees. She did, however, offer me a goodwill gesture (contradictory) of a free tub of dog food or to exchange the guinea pigs.

- Furthermore, the guinea pigs are sold in pairs, which was not mentioned when we called and was only confirmed on site.

- Finally, I should mention that one of the guinea pigs weighed barely more than 250g when we adopted it.

Given all of this, I cannot recommend this pet shop.
The staff were very helpful and friendly. We bought two guinea pigs that look to be in excellent health, directly from the owner's breeding farm.

We adopted two little rabbits: a Lionhead and a Lop. On August 22nd, they were already thriving! They settled in very well: less than 30 minutes after arriving in their new home, they were already eating hay and weren't even stressed by public transport. Truly calm little rabbits!

They live in complete freedom and don't cause any damage (except for electrical wires, which need to be well hidden). The little Lop, Nova, is adorable: so sweet and gentle. The Lionhead, Kali, has a bit of a personality, which makes her even cuter!

We are very happy with our two rabbits. Before them, we had a beloved little rabbit who passed away. Even though they can't replace her, they bring us so much joy now.

We don't regret adopting them at all; they are adorable.
I was very disappointed not to see a cat or dog, even though I could hear barking. That's not how they'll get adopted; it's seeing them that makes you fall in love.
Good pet shop, friendly service, easy to find.

Hello,
In April 2025, I bought Alto, a Maltipoo who is adorable and in excellent health. During his booster check-up, the vet found nothing wrong. I never thought I'd buy an animal from a breeder, but the breeder Alto came from treats their animals well, nothing like the factory farms that unfortunately still exist.
I received a warm welcome and I sometimes go back to buy supplies. Alto brings joy to the apartment...
I love them, I've known them since 1991
A small, well-hidden shop on Rue de la Pompe, with very original gadgets. Very friendly service.

We adopted a guinea pig that was sick. They refuse to cover the veterinary costs, even though the law prohibits the sale of sick animals. It's a crime, and despite the evidence, they offer no solution to the problem. They claim to monitor their animals, which is a lie; even the saleswoman hadn't noticed the little animal's condition. Avoid them at all costs—sick animals and completely irresponsible "sellers." We will be filing a complaint.
To my great disappointment, there were no cats or dogs like in the shop's photos. However, we received a fairly pleasant welcome. A little let down.

I adopted a British Shorthair.

Very calm and affectionate, with a beautiful white and grey coat, and I've had him for a month now – a very good experience.

I highly recommend this pet shop for the comprehensive support from Roxane and Héléna. They gave me a warm welcome and provided excellent advice on welcoming a puppy into our family. They even called me the following week to check in and answer my questions. We're still exchanging photos!
My puppy is very well-balanced, and we're experiencing absolute happiness as a family! It's clear the dogs are treated with care and attention!
Thank you, Héléna and Roxane!
For anyone looking for a dog, go there without hesitation!
Outrageous!!! It must be shut down immediately!!!!

We received an excellent welcome and were very well supported during the adoption of our little Spitz, and then our Chihuahua. We are overflowing with love and thank the two employees who were so lovely to us!

OUTRAGEOUS!

This pet shop has no regard for animal welfare!

The poor puppies are locked in a basement cellar, terrified and kept in deplorable sanitary conditions. Residents of the building complain about hearing them cry all night.

The owner couldn't care less about the animal welfare organizations that want to stop him from selling dogs. The traceability of the breeding program is also questionable.

Avoid this place for the sake of the dogs. Three people in my neighborhood had their dogs die very young, all from this shop.

It is with immense pleasure that I share my opinion. Starting with the lovely Helena who gave me such a warm welcome with her beautiful smile, not forgetting Roxanne and her kindness, it was their kindness that encouraged me to get my Shih Tzu. Big thanks, girls ❤️

A very playful and sociable Maltese.

He brings joy to the house.
Many thanks to the pet shop Les Animaux de Paris (16th arrondissement) for their work, and to the breeder in Mayenne.

I adopted a 4-month-old Maltese puppy in November 2023 from Les Animaux de Paris. I am delighted with them so far; my dog ​​is a little sweetheart. The welcome was warm and the advice was excellent. The animals are well cared for because he had already learned some commands like sit, down, stand, and heel. Thank you to the whole team; thanks to you, our family has found our happiness.
Listen, excellent advice, a lovely, happy dog ​​with his needs respected. Thank you again for your kindness and the care you give to the animals.

A disappointing experience and a serious compliance issue

I went to this pet store with my four-month-old Labrador to buy him a toy. The service was adequate, and the saleswoman seemed friendly at first.

Once home, I gave the toy to my dog, and in barely ten minutes, it was ripped open. Upon examination, I discovered it contained foam, which my veterinarian identified as toxic. Looking more closely, it turned out to be a children's toy, not one designed for dogs.

So I returned to the pet store to report the problem and request a refund or exchange. The response I received was, to say the least, surprising: they suggested I throw the toy away, but no refund or replacement was offered.

This pet store used to be a trusted one for me, but after this experience, I can no longer recommend it. The lack of consideration and the total absence of taking responsibility have definitively dissuaded me from returning.

A perfect experience from start to finish! The pet shop is well-run and the staff are passionate about animals. They patiently and kindly advised me and answered all my questions. My fluffy little French bulldog is in perfect health and already well-socialized. I sincerely thank Roxanne for her warm welcome, her availability, and all her invaluable advice!
I adopted a rabbit, and I was truly delighted with the discussions and advice I received about the adoption. The pet shop is very clean and we were made to feel very welcome!

Superb pet shop! Roxane and her colleague love animals. You can feel it and see it. We got a little rabbit named Popeye, and we're so happy with him. He's in great shape, very curious, and very intelligent. You can tell he's been well cared for. I highly recommend this pet shop.

Impeccable!!!
The staff are exceptionally kind.
Very clean place where the dogs are well treated…
A bit ridiculous, I admit:
My "beloved" Chihuahua gets her nails trimmed there every month!!!
A very kind and professional young woman. She loves her work. I highly recommend this shop.

I thank Les Animaux de Paris for their professionalism.
Thanks to you, I was able to acquire two magnificent Sacred Birman cats.

Today they are behaving wonderfully and get along perfectly!
I highly recommend this establishment!

We bought a beautiful Chartreux cat who is kind, gentle, etc.

We thank David, who has worked in this shop for years, for his excellent advice; …

I absolutely do not recommend this establishment for its business practices. We came to see a puppy that the whole family liked (my daughter was there and had fallen in love with the little dog). After noticing a bald patch on part of its …

I bought my dog ​​Moon from Les Animaux de Paris about two years ago. Even though Moon is an exceptional dog and I adore him, I have to say that my experience with this pet shop was truly disappointing. …
